title: The Bread in the Records
paras: Every Tuesday, food researcher Leila Costa visits the old [[court|court]] building in the [[central|central]] square of Bellara. Legal cases are no longer heard there, but its records remain. Leila studies complaints about bread from two hundred years ago. Her [[purpose|purpose]] is to discover what ordinary families actually ate.

There is [[plenty|plenty]] to learn from these complaints. One baker sold loaves that were too small; another added cheap bean flour. Other papers describe special bread for [[christian|Christian]] holidays. Leila is surprised by the [[variety|variety]]: some recipes contain dried apples, while others use potatoes. One letter even mentions river [[pollution|pollution]], which made the water unsuitable for baking.

In her small workshop, Leila tests the recipes with clean water and carefully measured ingredients. The results are not always [[impressive|impressive]]. Her first potato loaf was flat, and its thick outside was difficult to [[chew|chew]]. However, after several attempts, she produced a soft loaf with a pleasant taste. She wrote down every change so that others could repeat her work.

Last month, Leila shared this bread at an exhibition inside the former courtroom. Beside each slice, she placed a copy of an old complaint. Visitors laughed, tasted, and then read more closely. “[[hopefully|Hopefully]], they will remember the people behind these papers,” she said. By evening, only the papers were left.
zh: 每逢星期二，食品研究者莱拉·科斯塔都会到贝拉拉中央广场上的旧法院大楼去。那里已经不再审理案件，但档案仍保存着。莱拉研究的是两百年前人们对面包的投诉。她的目的是了解普通家庭当时究竟吃些什么。
这些投诉中有大量值得了解的信息。有个面包师出售的面包分量不足，另一个则掺入了廉价的豆粉。其他文件介绍了基督教节日期间食用的特殊面包。面包种类之多让莱拉惊讶：有些配方加入苹果干，另一些则使用土豆。一封信甚至提到了河水污染，导致河水不适合用来制作面包。
在自己的小工作室里，莱拉用干净的水和仔细称量过的原料试做这些配方。成品并不总是令人赞叹。她做的第一个土豆面包扁扁的，外皮很厚，难以咀嚼。不过，经过几次尝试，她做出了一个松软可口的面包。她记下每一处调整，以便别人也能照着制作。
上个月，莱拉在旧法庭内举办的一场展览上与大家分享了这种面包。每片面包旁边，她都放了一份旧投诉的复印件。参观者笑着品尝，然后更仔细地阅读起来。“希望他们会记住这些文件背后的人。”她说。到了傍晚，留下来的只有那些纸张。

q.s: The building Leila visits has stopped being used for legal hearings.
q.why: 首段说明那里已不再审理案件。

q.s: The outside of Leila's first potato loaf was easy to chew.
q.why: 原文明确说首次面包的厚外皮难以咀嚼。

q.s: Visitors paid an entrance fee to attend the exhibition.
q.why: 文章未提及展览是否收取门票。
